I am an old man in Mtwara, and groundnuts have been our crop here for many years. This small plot of less than half a hectare is close to the house, so my wife and children can help me weed and harvest when the time comes. I do not have money to waste on chemical fertilizer for nuts — groundnuts fix their own nitrogen, and the rains here are usually enough, so I will not irrigate. I will use seed I saved from last season and buy a little pesticide dust if the aphids come, but otherwise I rely on my own hands and maybe hire two or three people for harvesting and lifting the nuts.
